title: unify action usage summary scopes
status: design

branch: f_163_unify_action_usage_summary_scopes
worktree: 1
---

# Goal

Make `tokens`, `changes`, and `lines` in the card action popup use one explicit, user-selectable scope.

# Current state

`ActionUsageSummary` mixes scopes: tokens cover all loaded conversations for the action/card, changes cover only the displayed live or selected conversation, and lines cover commits from all runs in the action/card history. The labels do not explain this difference.

# Behavior

- Support two scopes:
  - **Conversation:** the displayed live or selected conversation. Match committed lines through the history entry whose `rootConversationId` equals the conversation id.
  - **Action/card:** all conversations and root-run history for the current action and card.
- Use action/card scope by default. A conversation selection change updates the conversation-scope values without changing the active scope.
- Always render all three values. Missing usage, file-change events, or commits count as zero for that metric and scope.
- Clicking any value toggles the shared scope and updates all three values together. Never allow different metrics to show different scopes.
- Render each value as a clearly interactive text control with pointer cursor, hover and keyboard-focus styling, and button semantics. Its accessible name includes the metric and active scope.
- Each metric has a tooltip that:
  - briefly defines the metric;
  - identifies the active scope and explains that clicking switches scope;
  - shows both the conversation and action/card values, marking the active one.
- `tokens` means cumulative provider token usage. `changes` means additions and deletions across completed provider file-change patches. `lines` means additions plus deletions in captured Git commit diffs.
- Keep the existing commit/file breakdown in the lines tooltip after the scope values, limited to commits in the active scope.
- When no conversation is displayed, use action/card scope and show conversation values as unavailable; do not toggle to an unavailable scope.

# Implementation

- Add one popup-bound usage-scope store beside the existing conversation and history stores; `ActionUsageSummaryOwner` subscribes with `useSyncExternalStore`.
- Add scoped aggregators for token usage, provider file changes, and commit line usage. Include the live conversation in action/card totals once, deduplicated by conversation id.
- Derive conversation commits from `AgentActionRunHistoryEntry.rootConversationId`; do not infer ownership from timestamps or commit paths.
- Update `ActionUsageSummary`, its owner, popup bindings, and focused tests. No persistence or Electron bridge changes are required.

# Acceptance criteria

- Tokens, changes, and lines always display the same active scope and switch together when any value is clicked or keyboard-activated.
- Every value visibly appears interactive and its tooltip explains the metric, switching behavior, and both scope values.
- Conversation scope uses only the displayed conversation and its matching commits; action/card scope includes every matching conversation and root run without double-counting the live conversation.
- Zero and unavailable states, live updates, conversation switching, commit matching, tooltips, pointer interaction, and keyboard interaction are covered by tests.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |

The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges. ## File naming | Decision | Rule | Rationale | | --- | --- | --- | | Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. | ## Services and state | Decision | Rule | Rationale | | --- | --- | --- | | Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. | | Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. The boundary between them is hard, and it is decided by location, not by content: - Markdown files in the **root of the working folder** are always cards. They must have an `internalId`; one is generated and persisted when missing. - Markdown files in the **archived or releases folder** are former cards and already carry an `internalId`. A file there *without* an `internalId` is a regular markdown file. - **Any other** markdown file in the project is a regular markdown file. It never receives an `internalId`, and loading a project must not rewrite it. Consequences: - `after:` chains only ever link cards, so every participant in a chain has an `internalId`. - Regular markdown files are identified by path alone, everywhere. - A regular markdown file becomes a card only through an explicit user action that moves it into the working folder root; the `internalId` is written at that moment. When reading a file, it calculates: ```text relativePath = relative(repositoryRoot, absoluteFilePath) ``` When writing, it performs the reverse: ```text absoluteFilePath = join(repositoryRoot, relativePath) ``` Every resolved target is checked to ensure it remains inside the repository root: [git_commands.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/git/git_commands.js:25). Paths are then used for: - Loading files and assets. - Writing, deleting, staging, and committing files. - Moving files through explicit `fromPath â†’ toPath` requests. - Emitting filesystem-watch events. - Identifying action source JSON files. - Scoping action contexts through `context.file`. - Keeping `cardPath` as historical execution metadata, not ownership. - Locating card activity through stable `cardInternalId`. - Locking concurrent tracked actions per card path. - Recording changed files and commit metadata. Problem\n\nEach card has one activity JSON containing canonical conversations and completed root-action records. For agent actions, `records[].history.prompt` duplicates the user message and `records[].history.output` duplicates assistant output already stored in `conversations[].entries`.\n\nThis makes the schema unclear and increases already large activity files. The record should describe an execution and link to its conversation; it should not contain a second transcript.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `conversations[]` owns the complete ordered agent transcript, provider events, tool output, status, timing, and usage.\n- `records[]` owns one summary per completed root execution, including aggregate commits and all conversation ids produced by its action chain.\n- Agent and command executions share one required `history` shape containing `prompt` and `output`.\n- `loadActionRunHistory` reads only `records[]`, so the agent history row depends on the duplicated strings.\n- `conversationIds[]` includes conversations from root and child actions but does not identify which conversation belongs to the root action.\n\n## Requested changes\n\n1. Make action activity records explicitly distinguish an agent root action from a command root action.\n2. For an agent root record:\n - persist a required `rootConversationId` referring to a conversation in the same activity file;\n - retain execution metadata that is not owned by the conversation, such as root status, model/security configuration, timing, and commits;\n - do not persist prompt, assistant output, transcript fragments, or tool output on the record.\n3. Keep `conversationIds[]` when it is needed to associate all root and child agent conversations with one execution. Do not use its ordering to infer the root conversation.\n4. For a command root record, retain command and output data because no conversation owns it.\n5. Replace the shared agent/command `history` payload with discriminated record details. Do not add optional fields whose meaning changes by convention.\n6. Update `loadActionRunHistory` and its bridge types so:\n - command history continues to expose command output;\n - agent history exposes execution metadata and the root conversation reference without reconstructing or copying transcript text;\n - commit history and card diff behavior remain unchanged.\n7. Update the agent run-history UI to show agent status, configuration, time, and commits. The conversation UI remains the only transcript renderer.\n8. Remove `createAgentHistoryEntry` once no call site needs a duplicate agent payload. Keep command-history construction single-purpose.\n\n## Persistence and migration\n\nIntroduce one new canonical activity schema version. Provide an explicit one-time migration from the current schema:\n\n- Match an agent record to its root conversation by the record's `conversationIds`, `rootActionId`, and the conversation's `actionId`.\n- Fail clearly when the root conversation is missing or ambiguous; do not guess from array order.\n- Remove duplicated agent prompt/output only after the canonical conversation has been validated.\n- Preserve command history, commits, statuses, timestamps, origins, and child conversation associations exactly.\n- Do not retain an indefinite dual-schema parser or write both representations.\n\nCoordinate this migration with conversation `viewed` persistence so the activity schema is migrated once if both jobs are implemented together.\n\n## Edge cases\n\n- A command root action invokes one or more child agent actions: command history remains on the record and `conversationIds[]` retains the child conversations; `rootConversationId` is not present.\n- An agent root action invokes child agents: `rootConversationId` identifies only the root conversation while `conversationIds[]` retains every associated conversation.\n- A failed or cancelled agent produces no assistant message: the record still preserves execution status and non-transcript failure metadata; no empty duplicate output is introduced.\n- A continued conversation contains several turns: the record links to the canonical conversation and does not copy the latest turn into history.\n- Scheduled and project-scoped actions follow the same model in `project.json`.\n- Commit visibility, ordering, labels, and diff loading must not change.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Newly written agent activity records contain no prompt or output strings duplicated from their conversation.\n- Every agent root record has an unambiguous `rootConversationId` resolving within the same activity file.\n- Command records retain their command and output history.\n- Agent conversation rendering and continuation still use `conversations[]` as the only transcript source.\n- Agent run history and card commit history still show their existing non-transcript metadata and commits.\n- Existing activity data is migrated explicitly to the new canonical schema, after which only that schema is accepted and written.\n- Tests cover agent and command roots, mixed root/child chains, continuation, failure/cancellation, scheduled/project actions, migration failures, bridge results, history rendering, and unchanged commit/diff behavior.\n\n\r\n", design\releases\0_1_0\card__299444fe-cb8b-420f-a89d-3c3300bf249e.json:234: "output": "---\nauthor:\nid: F_141\ninternalId: 299444fe-cb8b-420f-a89d-3c3300bf249e\ntitle: remove duplicate agent history payload\nstatus: ready for implementation\nowner:\naffects:\n - shared/card_activity.mjs\n - shared/card_activity.d.mts\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_run_history.js\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_files.js\n - app/src/data/electron_action_bridge.ts\n - app/src/components/actions/action_run_history.tsx\nagents:\npolicy:\nafter: \nworktree: 1\n---\n\n## Problem\n\nEach card has one activity JSON containing canonical conversations and completed root-action records. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Investigation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\r\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\r\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\r\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\r\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\r\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\r\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\r\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\r\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\r\\n\\r\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\r\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\r\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\r\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\r\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\r\\n\\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: B_85\\r\\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n - Streaming updates replace the same event by `providerItemId`, changing its status from `inProgress` to `completed`. `ActionConversationChat` currently renders every reasoning event, so completed reasoning blocks remain visible during the live run and in reopened conversations. Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\\r\\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\\r\\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\\r\\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\\r\\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\\r\\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\\r\\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\\r\\n\\n===== F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_94\\r\\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\\r\\n\\r\\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\\r\\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\\r\\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\\r\\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\\r\\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\\r\\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\\r\\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\\r\\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\\r\\n\\n===== F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_95\\r\\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\\r\\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\\r\\n\\r\\nCard commit history reads tracked `/activity/card__.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\r\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not model it as a user action.\\r\\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\\r\\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\\r\\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\\r\\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\\r\\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\\r\\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\\r\\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\r\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\r\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\r\\n\\n===== F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_96\\r\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\\r\\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\\r\\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\\r\\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\\r\\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\\r\\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\\r\\n\\n===== F_98_worktree_vs_project_folder_placeholders.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_98\\r\\ninternalId: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\r\\ntitle: worktree vs project folder placeholders\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\n---\\r\\nWe have 'rootProjectFolder' placeholder. this currently maps to the folder that the agent is running on, so it could the the main project folder or a worktree. \\r\\n\\r\\nWe need to improve this and split it up in `worktree-folder` and 'project-folder' where the last one always references the main project folder while 'worktree-folder' references the folder that the agent is currently running in.\\r\\n\\r\\nAlso, we need to add the 'releases-folder' as well\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` exists in action prompt/command and diff-command placeholder sets.\\r\\n- Action execution resolves it to the execution checkout, which may be the opened project folder or a linked worktree. Diff commands resolve it to the opened project folder.\\r\\n- Action editor insertion controls and user documentation expose only the existing placeholder.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Replace `{{rootProjectFolder}}` everywhere with `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}`; do not keep a legacy alias.\\r\\n- `{{worktree-folder}}` resolves to the absolute execution checkout path. When no linked worktree is selected, it equals `{{project-folder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{project-folder}}` always resolves to the absolute opened repository path, including during linked-worktree execution.\\r\\n- Add `{{releases-folder}}`, resolving to the configured repository-relative releases path: `/`.\\r\\n- Support all three placeholders in action prompts, action commands, prompt preparation, diff commands, editor insertion controls, validation, and documentation.\\r\\n- Fail before process start when a required placeholder value is unavailable. Add tests for primary and linked-worktree execution, custom release paths, diff commands, insertion controls, and removed `{{rootProjectFolder}}` support.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Primary-checkout actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- Linked-worktree actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` to that worktree and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- `{{releases-folder}}` returns the configured path relative to repository root, independent of active checkout.\\r\\n- Action prompts, action commands, and diff commands use the same three folder placeholders.\\r\\n- Editors and documentation list the new placeholders and no longer list `{{rootProjectFolder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` is not resolved.\\r\\n\\n===== J_020_unify_agent_conversation_entries.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-020\\r\\ninternalId: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\ntitle: unify agent conversation messages and events into ordered entries\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - shared/agent_conversations.mjs\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_conversation.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_transcript.js\\r\\n - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/agents/card_agent_state.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: c5d963f2-ca43-419d-bc3c-972199b7e7cd\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace the parallel agent-conversation `messages` and `events` arrays with one canonical ordered `entries` array. Array position is ingestion order and is the only display order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis refactor must land before the action-popup rendering-isolation work. That work must consume the single entry list and must not preserve the current merge-and-sort path.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Conversation entry**: one ordered item in an agent conversation.\\r\\n- **Message entry**: user or assistant text.\\r\\n- **Event entry**: reasoning, tool use, command execution, diagnostics, failures, and lifecycle observations.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not use **activity** for a conversation entry, field, helper, component, or collection. `activity` remains valid only for the separate card/project activity-storage domain.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPersisted `AgentConversation` stores `messages` and `events` separately. Live execution repeats the split as `LiveAgentTurn.messages` and `LiveAgentTurn.activities`. Producers append or replace items in those separate collections, while chat and transcript consumers merge and sort them by `sequence` to reconstruct ingestion order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe split causes:\\r\\n\\r\\n- duplicate persisted and live representations;\\r\\n- inconsistent `event`/`activity` terminology;\\r\\n- repeated merge and sort work in consumers;\\r\\n- a rebuilt full `AgentConversation` projection in the popup controller;\\r\\n- ordering behavior owned by presentation code instead of the producer.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required model\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a discriminated union and one collection:\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts\\r\\n\\n===== J_021_derive_markdown_styles_globally.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-021\\r\\ninternalId: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\ntitle: derive active Markdown content styles once in the global theme\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_context.ts\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_provider.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_provider.test.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/theme/use_app_theme.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/editor/markdown_style_sx.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/config/markdown_style_preview.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild the active Markdown content styling once when the global Markdown style configuration changes. Components that render active Markdown consume the stable derived style and never rebuild it during unrelated renders.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job is independent of the action-popup subscription refactor and should land before performance verification of that refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\n`AppThemeProvider` owns `markdownStyleConfig`, but consumers receive only the raw configuration. Both `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` call `buildMarkdownContentSx(markdownStyleConfig)` in their render bodies. The builder creates a new nested MUI style object even when the configuration is unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n`MarkdownStylePreview` also calls the builder, but it renders an explicit configuration draft rather than the active global style.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Derive a stable `markdownContentSx` value in `AppThemeProvider` with `useMemo`, depending only on `markdownStyleConfig`.\\r\\n- Expose the derived value through `AppThemeContextValue` and its fallback value.\\r\\n- Make `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` consume `markdownContentSx` directly.\\r\\n- Do not call `buildMarkdownContentSx` from either component.\\r\\n- Keep `buildMarkdownContentSx` as a pure derivation function owned by the theme/style layer.\\r\\n- Memoize `MarkdownStylePreview`'s derived style by its explicit `config` prop. The preview cannot consume the active global style because it must show unsaved draft configuration.\\r\\n- Do not introduce a service class; this is a pure derived theme value.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Identity contract\\r\\n\\r\\n- `markdownContentSx` retains object identity across renders when `markdownStyleConfig` is unchanged.\\r\\n- Changing palette mode, popup state, editor content, conversation content, or unrelated configuration does not rebuild it.\\r\\n- Changing the active Markdown style configuration rebuilds it once and updates all active Markdown consumers.\\r\\n- Changing the preview's explicit draft configuration rebuilds only the preview value.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Testing implications\\r\\n\\r\\n- Theme-provider tests prove the derived style is exposed and retains identity across unrelated provider renders.\\r\\n- Theme-provider tests prove changing `markdownStyleConfig` replaces the derived value.\\r\\n\\n===== J_022_stabilize_action_prompt_drafts.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-022\\r\\ninternalId: 5b39ff1e-4bbc-4d50-b527-36e1d1faa6f5\\r\\ntitle: move action prompt drafts out of popup React state\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_prompt_draft.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_prompt.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_bottom_row.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_content.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nGive each action prompt draft one lifetime-stable external store. Typing, flushing, preparing, replacing, clearing, restoring, and remotely synchronizing a prompt must not place the prompt text or reset counters in `ActionPopupContent` or its controller React state.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job must land before the major action-popup ownership and subscription refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPrompt ownership is duplicated:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `useActionPopupController` stores prompt value, preparation status, and reset token in React state.\\r\\n- `ActionPopupContent` creates a new `ActionPromptDraft` whenever the controller prompt or reset token changes.\\r\\n- `ActionPromptDraft` buffers live editor values and supports a narrow bottom-row subscription.\\r\\n- `ActionExecutionService` separately stores prompt values, revisions, pending bridge writes, and remote prompt sessions.\\r\\n\\r\\nOrdinary typing already stays out of root React state because `MarkdownEditor.onLiveChange` writes to `ActionPromptDraft`. Editor flush still calls `setPromptState`, and external preparation/replacement/clear operations update root state and replace the draft object. Those paths rerender the complete popup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required ownership\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate one prompt-draft service that owns stable draft stores keyed by the action context and, when applicable, the active agent session. The service is justified because it owns state, draft lifecycle, asynchronous bridge synchronization, revisions, and pending writes.\\r\\n\\r\\nMove the current prompt-draft map and remote prompt-session behavior out of `ActionExecutionService`. The renamed run/session service planned by the later popup refactor must not retain prompt text ownership.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach stable draft store exposes, at minimum:\\r\\n\\r\\n- current Markdown value;\\r\\n- preparation state: `loading`, `ready`, or `failed`;\\r\\n- a narrow subscription contract suitable for `useSyncExternalStore`;\\r\\n- local edit without React parent state;\\r\\n- external replacement that notifies the editor to call `setMarkdown` once;\\r\\n- clear, flush/synchronize, send, and current-value reads;\\r\\n- revision protection for superseded asynchronous preparation and remote writes.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not add arbitrary retention limits or silent eviction. Draft removal must follow explicit lifecycle events such as successful send, deliberate clear, action removal, or project teardown. A popup unmount does not discard an unsent draft.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== J_023_use_one_agent_conversation_model.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-023\\r\\ninternalId: 1244ac27-293a-4a5f-b478-0890ecc3fea6\\r\\ntitle: use one agent conversation model while growing and persisted\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_execution.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 5b39ff1e-4bbc-4d50-b527-36e1d1faa6f5\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nFollow J-020 by removing the remaining `LiveAgentTurn` model. A growing conversation and a persisted conversation are the same `AgentConversation`; persistence is only a lifecycle state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current problem\\r\\n\\r\\nJ-020 unified conversation content into `entries`, but renderer run state still stores `LiveAgentTurn`. `useActionPopupController` converts that object into a new `AgentConversation` during rendering. This duplicates models, metadata, and ownership.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Remove `LiveAgentTurn` and `liveAgentConversation`.\\r\\n- Store `AgentConversation | null` directly in run state.\\r\\n- Make the agent-start event provide the complete canonical conversation snapshot, including identity, metadata, path, status, and initial entries.\\r\\n- Apply later message/event updates immutably to that conversation's `entries` without changing entry order.\\r\\n- Apply status and completion metadata to the same model.\\r\\n- Persist and reload the same `AgentConversation` shape.\\r\\n- Continuation starts from the canonical source conversation and adds new entries without a renderer-side merge.\\r\\n- Do not add live/persisted adapters, compatibility shapes, or duplicated fields.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] `LiveAgentTurn` and `liveAgentConversation` no longer exist.\\r\\n- [ ] Growing, completed, persisted, loaded, and continued conversations all use `AgentConversation`.\\r\\n- [ ] Run state exposes the canonical conversation directly.\\r\\n- [ ] Popup rendering performs no conversation-shape conversion or history merge.\\r\\n- [ ] Entry identity and order remain stable during streamed updates.\\r\\n- [ ] App and desktop lint and tests pass.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Dependency\\r\\n\\r\\nJ-020 must be implemented first.\\r\\n\\n===== J_024_replace_execution_state_with_scoped_action_runs.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-024\\r\\ninternalId: 1975a005-f0bb-432f-8ecb-bc85a27819d2\\r\\ntitle: replace global execution state with scoped action runs\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/electron_action_bridge.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/hooks/use_action_executions.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_execution.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/shell/preload.js\\r\\n - shared/card_activity.mjs\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 1244ac27-293a-4a5f-b478-0890ecc3fea6\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace execution terminology and the global renderer snapshot with action-run terminology, a routing registry, and stable scoped run stores.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- `runId`, not `executionId`.\\r\\n- `ActionRun`, not `LiveActionExecution` or action execution.\\r\\n- `ActionRunRegistry`, not `ActionExecutionService`.\\r\\n- `ActionRunStore`: stable state owner for one run.\\r\\n- `runs`, not `executions`.\\r\\n- `ConversationEntry` remains reserved for items inside an agent conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\nRename the contract consistently across Electron, bridge messages, renderer services, hooks, persisted action records, errors, and tests. Process execution may keep that term only where it refers to an operating-system process.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Registry shape\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionRunRegistry` keeps one renderer-wide bridge subscription and a routing map from `runId` to stable `ActionRunStore`. The map is an internal index, not a React snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach `ActionRunStore` owns one run's status, logs, root action, active chained action, context, conversation, approvals, and question. Unrelated run changes must preserve selected store snapshots and must not render their consumers.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Persistence and lifecycle\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== J_025_move_action_popup_state_to_leaf_owners.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-025\\r\\ninternalId: 96705093-a302-409d-b626-fe3e16fd28e2\\r\\ntitle: move action popup state and subscriptions to leaf owners\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_content.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_selector.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_log_error_display.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_approval.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_question.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_bottom_row.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 1975a005-f0bb-432f-8ecb-bc85a27819d2\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nMake popup roots own layout and selection only. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Investigation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\r\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\r\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\r\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\r\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\r\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\r\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\r\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\r\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\r\\n\\r\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\r\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\r\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\r\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\r\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\r\\n\\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: B_85\\r\\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n - Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\\r\\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\\r\\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\\r\\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\\r\\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\\r\\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\\r\\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\\r\\n\\n===== F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_94\\r\\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\\r\\n\\r\\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. Keep command actions unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\\r\\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\\r\\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\\r\\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\\r\\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\\r\\n\\n===== F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_95\\r\\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\\r\\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\\r\\n\\r\\nCard commit history reads tracked `/activity/card__.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\r\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\\r\\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\\r\\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\\r\\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\\r\\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\\r\\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\\r\\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\r\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\r\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\r\\n\\n===== F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_96\\r\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\\r\\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\\r\\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\\r\\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\\r\\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\\r\\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\\r\\n\\n===== F_98_worktree_vs_project_folder_placeholders.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_98\\r\\ninternalId: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\r\\ntitle: worktree vs project folder placeholders\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\n---\\r\\nWe have 'rootProjectFolder' placeholder. this currently maps to the folder that the agent is running on, so it could the the main project folder or a worktree. \\r\\n\\r\\nWe need to improve this and split it up in `worktree-folder` and 'project-folder' where the last one always references the main project folder while 'worktree-folder' references the folder that the agent is currently running in.\\r\\n\\r\\nAlso, we need to add the 'releases-folder' as well\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` exists in action prompt/command and diff-command placeholder sets.\\r\\n- Action execution resolves it to the execution checkout, which may be the opened project folder or a linked worktree. Diff commands resolve it to the opened project folder.\\r\\n- Action editor insertion controls and user documentation expose only the existing placeholder.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Replace `{{rootProjectFolder}}` everywhere with `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}`; do not keep a legacy alias.\\r\\n- `{{worktree-folder}}` resolves to the absolute execution checkout path. When no linked worktree is selected, it equals `{{project-folder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{project-folder}}` always resolves to the absolute opened repository path, including during linked-worktree execution.\\r\\n- Add `{{releases-folder}}`, resolving to the configured repository-relative releases path: `/`.\\r\\n- Support all three placeholders in action prompts, action commands, prompt preparation, diff commands, editor insertion controls, validation, and documentation.\\r\\n- Fail before process start when a required placeholder value is unavailable. Add tests for primary and linked-worktree execution, custom release paths, diff commands, insertion controls, and removed `{{rootProjectFolder}}` support.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Primary-checkout actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- Linked-worktree actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` to that worktree and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- `{{releases-folder}}` returns the configured path relative to repository root, independent of active checkout.\\r\\n- Action prompts, action commands, and diff commands use the same three folder placeholders.\\r\\n- Editors and documentation list the new placeholders and no longer list `{{rootProjectFolder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` is not resolved.\\r\\n\\n===== J_020_unify_agent_conversation_entries.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-020\\r\\ninternalId: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\ntitle: unify agent conversation messages and events into ordered entries\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - shared/agent_conversations.mjs\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_conversation.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_transcript.js\\r\\n - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/agents/card_agent_state.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: c5d963f2-ca43-419d-bc3c-972199b7e7cd\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace the parallel agent-conversation `messages` and `events` arrays with one canonical ordered `entries` array. Array position is ingestion order and is the only display order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis refactor must land before the action-popup rendering-isolation work. That work must consume the single entry list and must not preserve the current merge-and-sort path.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Conversation entry**: one ordered item in an agent conversation.\\r\\n- **Message entry**: user or assistant text.\\r\\n- **Event entry**: reasoning, tool use, command execution, diagnostics, failures, and lifecycle observations.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not use **activity** for a conversation entry, field, helper, component, or collection. `activity` remains valid only for the separate card/project activity-storage domain.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPersisted `AgentConversation` stores `messages` and `events` separately. Live execution repeats the split as `LiveAgentTurn.messages` and `LiveAgentTurn.activities`. Producers append or replace items in those separate collections, while chat and transcript consumers merge and sort them by `sequence` to reconstruct ingestion order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe split causes:\\r\\n\\r\\n- duplicate persisted and live representations;\\r\\n- inconsistent `event`/`activity` terminology;\\r\\n- repeated merge and sort work in consumers;\\r\\n- a rebuilt full `AgentConversation` projection in the popup controller;\\r\\n- ordering behavior owned by presentation code instead of the producer.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required model\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a discriminated union and one collection:\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts\\r\\n\\n===== J_021_derive_markdown_styles_globally.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-021\\r\\ninternalId: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\ntitle: derive active Markdown content styles once in the global theme\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_context.ts\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_provider.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_provider.test.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/theme/use_app_theme.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/editor/markdown_style_sx.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/config/markdown_style_preview.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild the active Markdown content styling once when the global Markdown style configuration changes. Components that render active Markdown consume the stable derived style and never rebuild it during unrelated renders.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job is independent of the action-popup subscription refactor and should land before performance verification of that refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\n`AppThemeProvider` owns `markdownStyleConfig`, but consumers receive only the raw configuration. Both `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` call `buildMarkdownContentSx(markdownStyleConfig)` in their render bodies. The builder creates a new nested MUI style object even when the configuration is unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n`MarkdownStylePreview` also calls the builder, but it renders an explicit configuration draft rather than the active global style.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Derive a stable `markdownContentSx` value in `AppThemeProvider` with `useMemo`, depending only on `markdownStyleConfig`.\\r\\n- Expose the derived value through `AppThemeContextValue` and its fallback value.\\r\\n- Make `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` consume `markdownContentSx` directly.\\r\\n- Do not call `buildMarkdownContentSx` from either component.\\r\\n- Keep `buildMarkdownContentSx` as a pure derivation function owned by the theme/style layer.\\r\\n- Memoize `MarkdownStylePreview`'s derived style by its explicit `config` prop. The preview cannot consume the active global style because it must show unsaved draft configuration.\\r\\n- Do not introduce a service class; this is a pure derived theme value.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Identity contract\\r\\n\\r\\n- `markdownContentSx` retains object identity across renders when `markdownStyleConfig` is unchanged.\\r\\n- Changing palette mode, popup state, editor content, conversation content, or unrelated configuration does not rebuild it.\\r\\n- Changing the active Markdown style configuration rebuilds it once and updates all active Markdown consumers.\\r\\n- Changing the preview's explicit draft configuration rebuilds only the preview value.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Testing implications\\r\\n\\r\\n- Theme-provider tests prove the derived style is exposed and retains identity across unrelated provider renders.\\r\\n- Theme-provider tests prove changing `markdownStyleConfig` replaces the derived value.\\r\\n\\n===== J_022_stabilize_action_prompt_drafts.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-022\\r\\ninternalId: 5b39ff1e-4bbc-4d50-b527-36e1d1faa6f5\\r\\ntitle: move action prompt drafts out of popup React state\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_prompt_draft.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_prompt.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_bottom_row.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_content.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nGive each action prompt draft one lifetime-stable external store. Typing, flushing, preparing, replacing, clearing, restoring, and remotely synchronizing a prompt must not place the prompt text or reset counters in `ActionPopupContent` or its controller React state.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job must land before the major action-popup ownership and subscription refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPrompt ownership is duplicated:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `useActionPopupController` stores prompt value, preparation status, and reset token in React state.\\r\\n- `ActionPopupContent` creates a new `ActionPromptDraft` whenever the controller prompt or reset token changes.\\r\\n- `ActionPromptDraft` buffers live editor values and supports a narrow bottom-row subscription.\\r\\n- `ActionExecutionService` separately stores prompt values, revisions, pending bridge writes, and remote prompt sessions.\\r\\n\\r\\nOrdinary typing already stays out of root React state because `MarkdownEditor.onLiveChange` writes to `ActionPromptDraft`. Editor flush still calls `setPromptState`, and external preparation/replacement/clear operations update root state and replace the draft object. Those paths rerender the complete popup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required ownership\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate one prompt-draft service that owns stable draft stores keyed by the action context and, when applicable, the active agent session. The service is justified because it owns state, draft lifecycle, asynchronous bridge synchronization, revisions, and pending writes.\\r\\n\\r\\nMove the current prompt-draft map and remote prompt-session behavior out of `ActionExecutionService`. The renamed run/session service planned by the later popup refactor must not retain prompt text ownership.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach stable draft store exposes, at minimum:\\r\\n\\r\\n- current Markdown value;\\r\\n- preparation state: `loading`, `ready`, or `failed`;\\r\\n- a narrow subscription contract suitable for `useSyncExternalStore`;\\r\\n- local edit without React parent state;\\r\\n- external replacement that notifies the editor to call `setMarkdown` once;\\r\\n- clear, flush/synchronize, send, and current-value reads;\\r\\n- revision protection for superseded asynchronous preparation and remote writes.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not add arbitrary retention limits or silent eviction. Draft removal must follow explicit lifecycle events such as successful send, deliberate clear, action removal, or project teardown. A popup unmount does not discard an unsent draft.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== J_023_use_one_agent_conversation_model.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-023\\r\\ninternalId: 1244ac27-293a-4a5f-b478-0890ecc3fea6\\r\\ntitle: use one agent conversation model while growing and persisted\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_execution.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 5b39ff1e-4bbc-4d50-b527-36e1d1faa6f5\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nFollow J-020 by removing the remaining `LiveAgentTurn` model. A growing conversation and a persisted conversation are the same `AgentConversation`; persistence is only a lifecycle state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current problem\\r\\n\\r\\nJ-020 unified conversation content into `entries`, but renderer run state still stores `LiveAgentTurn`. `useActionPopupController` converts that object into a new `AgentConversation` during rendering. This duplicates models, metadata, and ownership.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Remove `LiveAgentTurn` and `liveAgentConversation`.\\r\\n- Store `AgentConversation | null` directly in run state.\\r\\n- Make the agent-start event provide the complete canonical conversation snapshot, including identity, metadata, path, status, and initial entries.\\r\\n- Apply later message/event updates immutably to that conversation's `entries` without changing entry order.\\r\\n- Apply status and completion metadata to the same model.\\r\\n- Persist and reload the same `AgentConversation` shape.\\r\\n- Continuation starts from the canonical source conversation and adds new entries without a renderer-side merge.\\r\\n- Do not add live/persisted adapters, compatibility shapes, or duplicated fields.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] `LiveAgentTurn` and `liveAgentConversation` no longer exist.\\r\\n- [ ] Growing, completed, persisted, loaded, and continued conversations all use `AgentConversation`.\\r\\n- [ ] Run state exposes the canonical conversation directly.\\r\\n- [ ] Popup rendering performs no conversation-shape conversion or history merge.\\r\\n- [ ] Entry identity and order remain stable during streamed updates.\\r\\n- [ ] App and desktop lint and tests pass.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Dependency\\r\\n\\r\\nJ-020 must be implemented first.\\r\\n\\n===== J_024_replace_execution_state_with_scoped_action_runs.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-024\\r\\ninternalId: 1975a005-f0bb-432f-8ecb-bc85a27819d2\\r\\ntitle: replace global execution state with scoped action runs\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/electron_action_bridge.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/hooks/use_action_executions.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_execution.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/shell/preload.js\\r\\n - shared/card_activity.mjs\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 1244ac27-293a-4a5f-b478-0890ecc3fea6\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace execution terminology and the global renderer snapshot with action-run terminology, a routing registry, and stable scoped run stores.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- `runId`, not `executionId`.\\r\\n- `ActionRun`, not `LiveActionExecution` or action execution.\\r\\n- `ActionRunRegistry`, not `ActionExecutionService`.\\r\\n- `ActionRunStore`: stable state owner for one run.\\r\\n- `runs`, not `executions`.\\r\\n- `ConversationEntry` remains reserved for items inside an agent conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\nRename the contract consistently across Electron, bridge messages, renderer services, hooks, persisted action records, errors, and tests. Process execution may keep that term only where it refers to an operating-system process.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Registry shape\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionRunRegistry` keeps one renderer-wide bridge subscription and a routing map from `runId` to stable `ActionRunStore`. The map is an internal index, not a React snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach `ActionRunStore` owns one run's status, logs, root action, active chained action, context, conversation, approvals, and question. Unrelated run changes must preserve selected store snapshots and must not render their consumers.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Persistence and lifecycle\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== J_025_move_action_popup_state_to_leaf_owners.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-025\\r\\ninternalId: 96705093-a302-409d-b626-fe3e16fd28e2\\r\\ntitle: move action popup state and subscriptions to leaf owners\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_content.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_selector.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_log_error_display.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_approval.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_question.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_bottom_row.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 1975a005-f0bb-432f-8ecb-bc85a27819d2\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nMake popup roots own layout and selection only. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\n\\n## Implementation details\\n\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not fast-forward or retain the card branch's individual commits on the project branch.\\n- Resolve the integration commit's activity metadata, then append one system activity record containing only that commit and labeled `Integrate into project` to the card's primary-checkout activity file. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\n\\r\\n\\n===== design\\\\releases\\\\0_0_4\\\\F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\r\\n---\\nauthor: \\nid: F_96\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\nstatus: ready\\nowner: \\naffects:\\nagents:\\npolicy:\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\n---\\n\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\n\\n# Current state\\n\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. They must have an `internalId`; one is generated and persisted when missing. - Markdown files in the **archived or releases folder** are former cards and already carry an `internalId`. A file there *without* an `internalId` is a regular markdown file. - **Any other** markdown file in the project is a regular markdown file. It never receives an `internalId`, and loading a project must not rewrite it. Consequences: - `after:` chains only ever link cards, so every participant in a chain has an `internalId`. - Regular markdown files are identified by path alone, everywhere. - A regular markdown file becomes a card only through an explicit user action that moves it into the working folder root; the `internalId` is written at that moment. Electron retains some transient stateâ€”current project, running executions, locks, schedules, watchersâ€”but not the rendererâ€™s complete card snapshot. ## Cards versus regular markdown files A project folder contains both cards and ordinary markdown documents. The boundary between them is hard, and it is decided by location, not by content: - Markdown files in the **root of the working folder** are always cards. They must have an `internalId`; one is generated and persisted when missing. - Markdown files in the **archived or releases folder** are former cards and already carry an `internalId`. A file there *without* an `internalId` is a regular markdown file. - **Any other** markdown file in the project is a regular markdown file. It never receives an `internalId`, and loading a project must not rewrite it. Consequences: - `after:` chains only ever link cards, so every participant in a chain has an `internalId`. - Regular markdown files are identified by path alone, everywhere. - A regular markdown file becomes a card only through an explicit user action that moves it into the working folder root; the `internalId` is written at that moment.
